stem: Which substance is stored in adipose tissue?
rationale: Fat is stored in adipose tissue. Adipose tissue serves as a thermal insulator in the subcutaneous tissues.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is transported by lipids?
rationale: Lipids are transported in the blood combined with proteins in lipoprotein particles. Lipids have essential roles in nutrition and health.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is required for the synthesis of prostaglandins?
rationale: Prostaglandins are synthesized in vivo by cyclizing the center of the carbon chain of 20-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acids. Arachidonic acid is a 20-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > FATTY ACIDS ARE ALIPHATIC CARBOXYLIC ACIDS > Unsaturated Fatty Acids Contain One or More Double Bonds

stem: Which substance are leukotrienes converted into?
rationale: Leukotrienes are eicosanoid derivatives formed via the lipoxygenase pathway (Figure 23–12).
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > FATTY ACIDS ARE ALIPHATIC CARBOXYLIC ACIDS > Unsaturated Fatty Acids Contain One or More Double Bonds

stem: Which substance are lipoxins converted into?
rationale: Lipoxins are eicosanoid derivatives formed via the lipoxygenase pathway (Figure 23–12).
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > FATTY ACIDS ARE ALIPHATIC CARBOXYLIC ACIDS > Unsaturated Fatty Acids Contain One or More Double Bonds

stem: Which substrate does lipoxygenase act on?
rationale: Leukotrienes are eicosanoid derivatives formed via the lipoxygenase pathway (Figure 23–12).
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > FATTY ACIDS ARE ALIPHATIC CARBOXYLIC ACIDS > Unsaturated Fatty Acids Contain One or More Double Bonds

stem: Which substance are phosphatidylcholines converted into?
rationale: Glycerophospholipids containing choline, known as phosphatidylcholines or lecithins, are the most abundant phospholipids in cell membranes. Phosphatidylcholines represent a large proportion of the body's store of choline.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > PHOSPHOLIPIDS ARE THE MAIN LIPID CONSTITUENTS OF MEMBRANES > Phosphatidylcholines (Lecithins) & Sphingomyelins Are Abundant in Cell Membranes

stem: Which substance is phosphatidic acid converted into?
rationale: Phosphatidic acid is a precursor of phosphatidylglycerol.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > PHOSPHOLIPIDS ARE THE MAIN LIPID CONSTITUENTS OF MEMBRANES > Cardiolipin Is a Major Lipid of Mitochondrial Membranes

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of mitochondrial dysfunction?
rationale: Alterations in cardiolipin structure cause mitochondrial dysfunction.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > PHOSPHOLIPIDS ARE THE MAIN LIPID CONSTITUENTS OF MEMBRANES > Cardiolipin Is a Major Lipid of Mitochondrial Membranes

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of atherosclerosis?
rationale: Lysophosphatidylcholine has been implicated in the effects of oxidized lipoproteins in promoting atherosclerosis.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > PHOSPHOLIPIDS ARE THE MAIN LIPID CONSTITUENTS OF MEMBRANES > Lysophospholipids Are Intermediates in the Metabolism of Phosphoglycerols

stem: Galactosylceramide is converted into which substance?
rationale: Galactosylceramide can be converted to sulfogalactosylceramide (sulfatide).
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Glucosylceramide is predominantly found within which structure?
rationale: Glucosylceramide is the predominant simple glycosphingolipid of extraneural tissues.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Glucosylceramide is converted into which substance?
rationale: Gangliosides are complex glycosphingolipids derived from glucosylceramide. Gangliosides contain one or more molecules of sialic acid.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Neuraminic acid is found within which structure?
rationale: Neuraminic acid (NeuAc) is the principal sialic acid found in human tissues. Gangliosides are present in nervous tissues in high concentration.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Ganglioside is predominantly found within which structure?
rationale: Gangliosides are present in nervous tissues in high concentration. Gangliosides function in cell-cell recognition and communication.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Monosialoganglioside is found within which structure?
rationale: GM1 is of considerable biologic interest as it is known to be the receptor in human intestine for cholera toxin. Other gangliosides can contain anywhere from one to five molecules of sialic acid, giving rise to di-, trisialogangliosides, etc.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > GLYCOLIPIDS (GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS) ARE IMPORTANT IN NERVE TISSUES & IN THE CELL MEMBRANE

stem: Bile acids are converted into which substance?
rationale: Cholesterol is the precursor of a large number of important steroids including bile acids, adrenocortical hormones, sex hormones, vitamin D, and cardiac glycosides.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > STEROIDS PLAY MANY PHYSIOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT ROLES

stem: Cholesterol is predominantly found within which structure?
rationale: Cholesterol is particularly abundant in nervous tissue.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > STEROIDS PLAY MANY PHYSIOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT ROLES > Cholesterol Is a Significant Constituent of Many Tissues

stem: Cholesterol is converted into which substance?
rationale: Cholesterol is often found as cholesteryl ester.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > STEROIDS PLAY MANY PHYSIOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT ROLES > Cholesterol Is a Significant Constituent of Many Tissues

stem: Five-carbon isoprene is converted into which substance?
rationale: Polyprenoids are not steroids but are related to them because they are synthesized from five-carbon isoprene units, like cholesterol (see Figure 26–2).
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > STEROIDS PLAY MANY PHYSIOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT ROLES > Polyprenoids Share the Same Parent Compound as Cholesterol

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of cancer?
rationale: Lipid peroxidation damage includes cancer, inflammatory diseases, atherosclerosis, and aging. Free radicals are molecules with unpaired valence electrons.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > LIPID PEROXIDATION IS A SOURCE OF FREE RADICALS

stem: Catalase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Preventive antioxidants include catalase and peroxidases like glutathione peroxidase, which react with ROOH.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > LIPID PEROXIDATION IS A SOURCE OF FREE RADICALS

stem: Peroxidases act on which substrate?
rationale: Preventive antioxidants include catalase and peroxidases like glutathione peroxidase, which react with ROOH.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > LIPID PEROXIDATION IS A SOURCE OF FREE RADICALS

stem: Selenium is an essential component of which substance?
rationale: Selenium is an essential component of glutathione peroxidase.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > LIPID PEROXIDATION IS A SOURCE OF FREE RADICALS

stem: Malondialdehyde is converted into which substance?
rationale: Malondialdehyde is formed by fatty acids with three or more double bonds.
citation: chapter_21_lipids_of_physiologic_significance — Lipids of Physiologic Significance > LIPID PEROXIDATION IS A SOURCE OF FREE RADICALS
